overview: Two fundamentally different ways atoms bond — one through complete electron transfer, the other through electron sharing.
genZNote: One bond is a full transfer. The other is a shared custody arrangement.

aspects.label: Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Complete transfer of electrons from one atom to another, forming oppositely charged ions held by electrostatic attraction.
aspects.valueB: Sharing of electron pairs between atoms.

aspects.label: Typically Formed Between
aspects.valueA: A metal and a nonmetal (large electronegativity difference).
aspects.valueB: Two nonmetals (small or no electronegativity difference).

aspects.label: Typical Physical Properties
aspects.valueA: High melting/boiling points, conduct electricity when molten/dissolved, often soluble in water.
aspects.valueB: Lower melting/boiling points, generally poor electrical conductors, variable water solubility.
